admission.justification: The packet explicitly rejects pytest-only detection and save/restore; refusing before mutation continues to bind new shared-support callers.

alternatives.option: One protected-path guard used before settings-parent creation and mutation, with a recursive syntactic regression test.
alternatives.reason: The boundary works for reusable support independently of whether pytest is running.

alternatives.option: Rely only on pytest detection or conftest moving configuration.
alternatives.reason: A standalone support caller can reach the live account settings without pytest isolation.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Support ceases to be reusable outside an enforceably isolated runner, with a new governing ruling.

alternatives.option: Save the live settings file, mutate it, then restore it.
alternatives.reason: It still writes the live file and can interrupt role transport or lose state before restoration.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The governing requirement is explicitly changed to permit live-file mutation.

consequences: Future shared-support settings mutations must obtain the guard path; product settings ownership stays unchanged.
context: A test-world call outside pytest overwrote the user settings file; pytest-only isolation did not protect reusable support.

evidence: MIK-R135@v1 Required Behavior 1-4 and nonconforming examples; CODE R4 verdict; originals and projection identities in producer-resolutions.json.
